payload.task_text:
The support operations team needs to create a customer feedback program based on actual support ticket data from the company data warehouse. The data warehouse contains a support center database with ticket records including issue types, priorities, response times, and customer satisfaction scores.

Start by querying the data warehouse to identify the top five issue types by total ticket volume from the SUPPORT_CENTER.PUBLIC.TICKETS table. For each of those five issue types, note the ticket count, average response time in hours, and average customer satisfaction score.

Next, create a Google Form titled "Customer Feedback Survey" with a description of "Help us improve our support services by sharing your feedback on recent issues." The form should contain at least five questions. Include a question asking which issue type the customer experienced, presented as a multiple choice question with the top five issue types as options. Include a question asking the customer to rate their overall satisfaction on a scale from 1 to 5. Include a question asking what could be improved about the support experience, as a free text response. Include a question asking how likely the customer is to recommend the support service to others on a scale of 1 to 10, as a free text or short answer question. Include a question asking for any additional comments or suggestions, as a free text response.

Then create an Excel workbook called Support_Feedback_Analysis.xlsx in the workspace with three sheets. The first sheet should be named "Ticket Analysis" and contain columns Issue_Type, Ticket_Count, Avg_Response_Time, and Avg_Satisfaction. Populate it with the top five issue types sorted by ticket count in descending order, where Avg_Response_Time is rounded to two decimal places and Avg_Satisfaction is rounded to two decimal places. The second sheet should be named "Priority Breakdown" and contain columns Priority, Count, Pct_of_Total, and Avg_Response_Time. Populate it with one row per priority level sorted alphabetically by priority name, where Pct_of_Total is the percentage of total tickets rounded to two decimal places and Avg_Response_Time is rounded to two decimal places. The third sheet should be named "Improvement Plan" and contain columns Issue_Type, Current_Satisfaction, Target_Satisfaction, and Action_Item. Populate it with the top five issue types sorted by ticket count in descending order. Current_Satisfaction should match the average satisfaction from the Ticket Analysis sheet. Target_Satisfaction should be the current satisfaction plus 0.5 rounded to two decimal places. Action_Item should contain a brief one-sentence description of a specific improvement action for that issue type. All numeric cells (Ticket_Count, Avg_Response_Time, Avg_Satisfaction, Count, Pct_of_Total, Current_Satisfaction, Target_Satisfaction) must be written as literal numeric values, not as Excel formulas.

Create a Word document called Support_Improvement_Report.docx in the workspace. The document should include a title "Support Service Improvement Report", an executive summary section that mentions the total number of tickets analyzed and the overall average satisfaction score, a key findings section that discusses the top issue types and their satisfaction scores, and an improvement recommendations section that outlines specific actions for each of the top five issue types.

Finally, send an email to support-team@company.com with the subject "Support Improvement Report - Action Required". The email body should include a summary of the key findings from the analysis, mentioning the total number of tickets, the top issue type by volume, and the overall average satisfaction score.

Task-Solving Rationable with Sub-task Decomposition:
To solve this task efficiently, the main agent first computes one compact canonical SQL payload, then launches three independent writers and the email branch together.

Use set-based read-only SQL against SUPPORT_CENTER.PUBLIC.TICKETS to obtain: the top five issue types by ticket count with average response time and satisfaction; every priority's count, percent of the same total and average response time; total ticket count; and overall average satisfaction. Preserve exact source issue/priority labels, use deterministic Issue_Type ascending tie-breaks after ticket count descending, and verify priority counts sum to the total. Freeze one canonical payload containing the Ticket Analysis rows, Priority Breakdown rows, Improvement Plan rows with target=current+0.5, Summary facts, exact form options, Word facts and email facts. No branch may rerun SQL or recompute metrics.

1. Wave 1 — dispatch exactly 3 coder sub-agents in parallel:

   1. coder 0 (office-report-builder 0): One Coder solely writes Support_Feedback_Analysis.xlsx in the dynamically resolved workspace. Create exactly Ticket Analysis, Priority Breakdown, and Improvement Plan with the task's exact headers/order, literal numeric values, rounding and all canonical rows; read every populated range back.
   2. coder 1 (office-report-builder 1): One Coder solely writes Support_Improvement_Report.docx from the canonical payload. Include the exact title, executive summary with total/overall satisfaction, key findings covering all top-five issues and satisfaction values, and one specific recommendation per issue; read full text/headings back.
   3. coder 2 (external-workflow-operator 0): One Coder owns exactly one Google Form creation. Call create_form with title Customer Feedback Survey and description Help us improve our support services by sharing your feedback on recent issues. exactly once and retain formId. Sequentially add: a multiple-choice issue question with the literal top-five issue options; a multiple-choice satisfaction question with options 1, 2, 3, 4, 5; a free-text improvement question; a short-text recommendation-likelihood question explicitly asking for 1-10; and a free-text additional-comments question. Then call get_form(formId) and verify the ordered titles/types/options. Never search for a form through unsupported tools or retry an ambiguous creation.

In the same response that launches Wave 1, the main agent searches Sent mail for complete To support-team@company.com / subject Support Improvement Report - Action Required. Read candidates to verify recipients, send exactly once only if absent using the literal total tickets, top issue and overall satisfaction from the canonical payload, and read it back.

After Wave 1, reconcile workbook, document, form and email independently against the same SQL payload, including exact form option order and all arithmetic. Do not dispatch a verification wave.

nodes.text:
Create a Google Form for a customer feedback program. You have access to Google Forms tools (mcp__google_forms__*).

Requirements:
1. Create a form with:
   - Title: "Customer Feedback Survey" (exactly this title)
   - Description: "Help us improve our support services by sharing your feedback on recent issues." (exactly this description)

2. Add at least five questions. Use exactly these five (you may add more if you wish, but these five are mandatory):

   a) MULTIPLE CHOICE question:
      Title: "Which issue type did you experience?"
      Options (exactly these 5): "Performance Issue", "Bug", "Feature Request", "Incident", "Service Request"
      (Mark it required if the tool supports it.)

   b) MULTIPLE CHOICE question (satisfaction rating):
      Title: "How would you rate your overall satisfaction with the support you received?"
      Options: "1", "2", "3", "4", "5"
      (This represents a 1 to 5 satisfaction scale, 1 = very dissatisfied, 5 = very satisfied.)

   c) FREE TEXT question:
      Title: "What could be improved about the support experience?"

   d) FREE TEXT / SHORT ANSWER question:
      Title: "How likely are you to recommend our support service to others, on a scale of 1 to 10 (1 = not at all likely, 10 = extremely likely)?"

   e) FREE TEXT question:
      Title: "Do you have any additional comments or suggestions?"

3. After creating, verify by calling get_form on the form ID to confirm the title, description, and questions are present.

Report back: the form ID, the confirmed title/description, and the list of questions present in the form. Use only the Google Forms tools; do not modify any other external system.
Create customer feedback Google Form

Create an Excel workbook at this exact path:
/workspace/dumps/kimi-code_Qwen3.8-Max/SingleUserTurn-gform-snowflake-feedback/workspace/Support_Feedback_Analysis.xlsx

The workbook must have exactly three sheets named "Ticket Analysis", "Priority Breakdown", and "Improvement Plan" (rename default sheets as needed). The data below comes from support ticket analysis of the data warehouse and is final — use these exact pre-rounded values, do not recompute or re-query anything.

CRITICAL REQUIREMENT: Every numeric cell (Ticket_Count, Avg_Response_Time, Avg_Satisfaction, Count, Pct_of_Total, Current_Satisfaction, Target_Satisfaction) must be written as a LITERAL numeric value (a real number), NOT as an Excel formula (no "=..." strings) and NOT as a text string. Header cells are text.

Sheet 1: "Ticket Analysis"
Header row (row 1): Issue_Type, Ticket_Count, Avg_Response_Time, Avg_Satisfaction
Data rows (sorted by Ticket_Count descending, exactly in this order):
Row 2: Performance Issue | 8128 | 15.20 | 3.38
Row 3: Bug | 6804 | 15.96 | 2.96
Row 4: Feature Request | 6118 | 14.63 | 3.31
Row 5: Incident | 4463 | 14.61 | 3.31
Row 6: Service Request | 3002 | 14.27 | 3.31
(Ticket_Count are integers; Avg_Response_Time and Avg_Satisfaction are numbers rounded to two decimal places as shown.)

Sheet 2: "Priority Breakdown"
Header row (row 1): Priority, Count, Pct_of_Total, Avg_Response_Time
Data rows (sorted alphabetically by priority name, exactly in this order):
Row 2: High | 6466 | 20.47 | 6.23
Row 3: Low | 9348 | 29.59 | 25.76
Row 4: Medium | 15774 | 49.94 | 12.28
(Count are integers; Pct_of_Total and Avg_Response_Time are numbers rounded to two decimal places.)

Sheet 3: "Improvement Plan"
Header row (row 1): Issue_Type, Current_Satisfaction, Target_Satisfaction, Action_Item
Data rows (sorted by ticket count descending, same order as Ticket Analysis):
Row 2: Performance Issue | 3.38 | 3.88 | Deploy proactive performance monitoring and caching optimizations to resolve latency-related tickets faster.
Row 3: Bug | 2.96 | 3.46 | Strengthen regression testing and introduce a structured bug triage process to reduce recurring defects.
Row 4: Feature Request | 3.31 | 3.81 | Create a transparent feature request pipeline with regular status updates for requesting customers.
Row 5: Incident | 3.31 | 3.81 | Implement automated incident detection and improve real-time customer communication during outages.
Row 6: Service Request | 3.31 | 3.81 | Streamline service request routing and expand the self-service knowledge base to speed fulfillment.
(Current_Satisfaction matches Ticket Analysis Avg_Satisfaction for the same issue type; Target_Satisfaction equals Current_Satisfaction + 0.5 rounded to two decimal places. Both must be literal numbers.)

Steps: create the workbook, create/rename the three sheets, write data with numeric cells as real numbers, optionally format headers bold for readability (formatting is optional, numeric literal correctness is mandatory).

After writing, verify by reading back the data from all three sheets. Report back: confirmation that the file exists at the exact path, the three sheet names, and the verified cell contents (especially confirming numeric cells contain literal numbers, e.g. 8128, 20.47, 3.88).
Build Support_Feedback_Analysis.xlsx

Create a Word document at this exact path:
/workspace/dumps/kimi-code_Qwen3.8-Max/SingleUserTurn-gform-snowflake-feedback/workspace/Support_Improvement_Report.docx

You have Word document tools (mcp__word__*) for creating documents, adding headings, and adding paragraphs. The content below is based on support ticket data analysis and is final — use it as given (you may lightly reword prose for flow, but all numbers and facts must be preserved exactly).

Document structure and content requirements:

1. Title (use a prominent heading/style): "Support Service Improvement Report"

2. Section: "Executive Summary" (Heading 1 or equivalent)
Content must explicitly mention the total number of tickets analyzed and the overall average satisfaction score. Write something like:
"This report analyzes a total of 31,588 support tickets from the company data warehouse to identify improvement opportunities in our support operations. Across all tickets, the overall average customer satisfaction score is 3.26 out of 5, with an average response time of 15.03 hours. The analysis reveals that Performance Issue, Bug, and Feature Request tickets dominate ticket volume, and that Bug tickets in particular drag down customer satisfaction. This report outlines targeted actions for each of the top five issue types to raise satisfaction toward a target of 0.5 points above current levels."

3. Section: "Key Findings" (Heading 1 or equivalent)
Discuss the top issue types and their satisfaction scores. Include these facts:
- Performance Issue is the most common issue type with 8,128 tickets, an average response time of 15.20 hours, and an average satisfaction score of 3.38.
- Bug is second with 6,804 tickets and has the lowest customer satisfaction among the top five at just 2.96, with the slowest average response time at 15.96 hours.
- Feature Request (6,118 tickets, satisfaction 3.31, response time 14.63 hours), Incident (4,463 tickets, satisfaction 3.31, response time 14.61 hours), and Service Request (3,002 tickets, satisfaction 3.31, response time 14.27 hours) round out the top five.
- By priority, Medium priority tickets make up 49.94% of volume (15,774 tickets), Low priority 29.59% (9,348 tickets), and High priority 20.47% (6,466 tickets). Low priority tickets have the slowest response time at 25.76 hours, while High priority tickets are answered fastest at 6.23 hours.

4. Section: "Improvement Recommendations" (Heading 1 or equivalent)
Outline specific actions for each of the top five issue types (one paragraph or bullet per issue type):
- Performance Issue: Deploy proactive performance monitoring and caching optimizations to resolve latency-related tickets faster.
- Bug: Strengthen regression testing and introduce a structured bug triage process to reduce recurring defects and lift the lowest satisfaction score (2.96).
- Feature Request: Create a transparent feature request pipeline with regular status updates for requesting customers.
- Incident: Implement automated incident detection and improve real-time customer communication during outages.
- Service Request: Streamline service request routing and expand the self-service knowledge base to speed fulfillment.
You may also add a closing sentence noting each issue type targets a satisfaction increase of 0.5 points (e.g., Performance Issue from 3.38 to 3.88).

After creating the document, verify it exists and re-read its text (e.g., with a get document text outline tool) to confirm the title and all three sections plus the key numbers (31,588 tickets, 3.26 satisfaction, top five issue types) are present.

Report back: the exact file path, confirmation it exists, and an outline of the headings/sections found.
Build Support_Improvement_Report.docx

Send one email using the available email tools (mcp__emails__*).

Recipient (To): support-team@company.com
Subject (exactly): Support Improvement Report - Action Required

Plain-text body (include a summary of key findings from the support ticket analysis — the numbers below are final, use them exactly):

"Hi Support Team,

Our customer feedback program analysis of support tickets from the data warehouse is complete. Below is a summary of the key findings:

- Total tickets analyzed: 31,588
- Overall average customer satisfaction score: 3.26 out of 5
- Overall average response time: 15.03 hours
- Top issue type by volume: Performance Issue, with 8,128 tickets (average satisfaction 3.38)

Top five issue types by ticket volume:
1. Performance Issue — 8,128 tickets (avg satisfaction 3.38)
2. Bug — 6,804 tickets (avg satisfaction 2.96, the lowest of the top five)
3. Feature Request — 6,118 tickets (avg satisfaction 3.31)
4. Incident — 4,463 tickets (avg satisfaction 3.31)
5. Service Request — 3,002 tickets (avg satisfaction 3.31)

A full Support Improvement Report and analysis workbook have been prepared, with a target of raising satisfaction by 0.5 points for each issue type. A Customer Feedback Survey is also being launched to collect direct customer input. Please review the recommended actions for your respective areas — your action is required.

Best regards,
Support Operations Team"

After sending, report back the send result/status. Send only this single email; do not send any other emails or perform other side effects.
Send support improvement email
